After months of testing Liquid Glass, WhatsApp is expanding user access to its redesigned iPad app interface, including a new Mac-like sidebar. Here's what you need to know.

WhatsApp is developing a brand-new iPad app interface

WhatsApp began working on adapting the Liquid Glass visual overhaul for its iOS app as early as last October, but the company only brought the redesign to the iPad at a later stage, starting limited beta testing in June.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the redesign included Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons and context menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar familiar from the iPhone.

WABetaInfo is now reporting that WhatsApp is rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the bottom tab bar by default with a brand-new Mac-like sidebar.

This sidebar mirrors the layout of the existing WhatsApp Mac app, providing quick access to Chats, Updates, Communities, Calls, Meta AI and other app sections. Users can also collapse it to give the conversation list and chat windows more display space.

WABetaInfo reports as follows:

WABetaInfo notes that some beta testers on the latest TestFlight build already have access to the new sidebar, and some users on the regular App Store version are also starting to see the change.

As is customary with WhatsApp, the new interface may take some time to roll out to all users, whether they're on the beta or the official version. However, once iPad users receive the update, they'll be able to benefit from a layout better suited to tablet use.
